title: Rapid sequence induction and failed intubation (adult)
subject: anaesthesia
setting: Operating theatre, emergency department, ICU, ward
summary: Plan and brief before induction, preoxygenate head-up to an end-tidal O2 of 0.9, give an induction agent and a full dose of rocuronium or suxamethonium without delay, intubate with a videolaryngoscope, confirm with waveform capnography, and move promptly through DAS Plans A to D if intubation fails.

sections.title: Assess and plan
items: RSI is for patients at increased risk of pulmonary aspiration (full stomach, bowel obstruction, upper GI bleed, pregnancy, emergency surgery, critically ill).

Assess anatomical difficulty (previous difficulty, Mallampati 3 or 4, limited mouth opening or neck movement, obesity, obstructive sleep apnoea) and physiological difficulty (hypoxaemia, hypotension, shock, severe acidosis, right heart failure).

MACOCHA score in critical care: Mallampati 3 or 4 (5 points), obstructive sleep apnoea (2), reduced neck mobility, mouth opening under 3 cm, coma, SpO2 under 80%, non-anaesthetist operator (1 each); 3 or more predicts difficulty.
If difficulty is predicted in any of Plans A to D, consider awake tracheal intubation or the most experienced operator, and decide in advance whether to wake the patient if intubation fails.
Mark the cricothyroid membrane (palpation or ultrasound) before induction when difficulty is anticipated.

sections.title: Preparation checklist
items: Use a checklist and a team brief: allocate roles (intubator, drugs, monitoring, cricoid force, equipment assistant, runner, second intubator) and state Plans A to D aloud.
Monitoring: SpO2 with audible tone, ECG, blood pressure, waveform capnography checked working before induction, end-tidal O2 where available.

Equipment: videolaryngoscope (first line), direct laryngoscope, bougie and stylet, two tube sizes, second-generation supraglottic airway (SAD), facemask and oropharyngeal and nasopharyngeal airways, suction on and at hand, eFONA kit (size 10 scalpel, bougie, size 6.0 cuffed tube).
Two working IV or IO lines; fluid running; vasopressor drawn up (for example phenylephrine or noradrenaline) and a team member nominated to manage haemodynamics.
Optimise before induction: resuscitate shock, treat severe hypoxaemia with CPAP or NIV, aspirate an existing nasogastric tube and leave it in place.
Start a timer when the neuromuscular blocker is given to prompt timely transitions.

sections.title: Preoxygenation and induction
items: Position head-up 30 degrees (ramped in obesity, ear level with sternal notch).

Preoxygenate with a tight-fitting facemask at 10 to 15 L/min of 100% O2 for at least 3 minutes (or 8 vital capacity breaths in 60 seconds), aiming for end-tidal O2 of 0.9. Use CPAP, NIV or high-flow nasal oxygen (HFNO) when hypoxaemic or difficulty is expected.
Continue oxygen during apnoea: standard nasal cannula at 15 L/min (5 L/min while awake) or HFNO over 30 L/min, with a patent airway.

Give the induction agent and the neuromuscular blocker in rapid succession without waiting to test mask ventilation. Choose and dose the induction agent by physiology: reduce the dose in shock or old age.
Use a neuromuscular blocker routinely: rocuronium 1.2 mg/kg or suxamethonium 1.5 mg/kg per DAS 2025. Either is acceptable when suxamethonium is not contraindicated.

Cricoid force (10 N awake, 30 N after loss of consciousness) by a trained assistant is optional; release it if the view is poor, if inserting a SAD, if mask ventilation is difficult or if the patient vomits.
Gentle low-pressure mask ventilation is acceptable in patients at risk of rapid desaturation.

sections.title: Plan A: intubation
items: Use a videolaryngoscope first line where available; with a hyperangulated blade always use a stylet, bougie or bronchoscope. Make the first attempt the best attempt.

Maximum 3 attempts, plus a fourth by a more experienced operator (3+1). Change something each time: position, blade or device, introducer, external laryngeal manipulation, suction, remove cricoid force, top up neuromuscular block.
Abandon any attempt if SpO2 falls and reoxygenate by facemask; keep the patient anaesthetised between attempts.
Confirm with a two-point check: sustained exhaled CO2 on waveform capnography plus seeing the tube pass the cords. No trace, wrong place.
After 3+1 failed attempts, or earlier if no improvement is possible, declare failed intubation aloud, call for help, go to Plan B and open or prime the eFONA kit.

sections.title: Plans B, C and D (CICO)
items: Plan B: insert a second-generation SAD, maximum 3 attempts. If oxygenation is effective, stop, think and communicate; the default is to wake the patient with full reversal.
Proceeding with the SAD, one flexible-bronchoscope-guided intubation through it, or a surgical airway are high-risk senior decisions. No blind intubation through a SAD.
Plan C: final attempt at facemask ventilation with full neuromuscular block, adequate anaesthesia, optimal position, oral and nasal airways and a two-person (four-handed) technique.

Can't intubate, can't oxygenate (CICO): declare it, allocate roles and proceed immediately to Plan D. Give a full dose of neuromuscular blocker first; if sugammadex was already given, use a blocker other than rocuronium or vecuronium.

Plan D, scalpel-bougie-tube: maximal neck extension and oxygen to the upper airway throughout. If the cricothyroid membrane is not clearly palpable, make a vertical midline skin incision up to 8 cm and blunt dissect to find it.

Stab the membrane transversely with a size 10 blade, rotate it 90 degrees, slide the bougie alongside into the trachea 10 to 15 cm, railroad a 6.0 cuffed tube, inflate and confirm with waveform capnography.
Sugammadex rescue of rocuronium is not a reliable CICO strategy (DAS 2025): it may not restore a patent airway and delays eFONA.

sections.title: After intubation
items: Secure the tube, note depth, check bilateral air entry and chest X-ray; insert a nasogastric tube.
Start sedation and analgesia promptly, especially after rocuronium, to prevent awareness under paralysis.
Anticipate post-intubation hypotension: avoid large tidal volumes, high rates and high PEEP initially, and treat with fluid and vasopressor.
Use lung-protective ventilation (tidal volume 6 to 8 mL/kg predicted body weight) and continuous capnography.
Document the airway difficulty, tell the patient in writing, and debrief the team after any failed intubation or eFONA.

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Underdosing the neuromuscular blocker, or giving it late: worsens intubating conditions and mask ventilation.
Full-dose propofol in a shocked patient; peri-intubation cardiac arrest is often from hypotension and hypoxaemia, not the airway.
Task fixation with repeated laryngoscopy instead of declaring failure and moving to the next plan.
Trusting chest rise, misting or auscultation instead of waveform capnography to exclude oesophageal intubation.
Suxamethonium in hyperkalaemia, burns or crush injury after the first day, rhabdomyolysis, denervation or neuromuscular disease, or malignant hyperthermia history.

drugs.name: Ketamine
drugs.notes: Favoured when haemodynamics are unstable (DAS ICU 2018); smaller doses in severe shock.

drugs.name: Etomidate
drugs.notes: Haemodynamically stable; single dose causes transient adrenal suppression. SCCM 2023 found no outcome difference versus other agents and suggests against routine steroids after it.

drugs.name: Propofol
drugs.dose: 1.5 to 2.5 mg/kg IV in fit adults; much lower titrated doses in elderly, shocked or septic patients
drugs.notes: Most hypotensive of the induction agents.

drugs.name: Thiopental (thiopentone)
drugs.notes: Still used for classic RSI in India; reduce in shock.

drugs.name: Rocuronium
drugs.notes: Intubating conditions in about 60 seconds; lasts 30 to 60 minutes or more, so give post-intubation sedation promptly.

drugs.name: Suxamethonium (succinylcholine)
drugs.notes: Short acting; contraindicated in hyperkalaemia, burns or crush after 24 hours, denervation, myopathy, malignant hyperthermia history.

drugs.name: Sugammadex
drugs.dose: 16 mg/kg IV for immediate reversal of rocuronium 1.2 mg/kg
drugs.notes: Draw up early if planning to wake; not a reliable rescue in CICO.
